articles.title: Home Assistant lets you choose automation triggers without naming them
articles.dek: The visual editor shows the events themselves and keeps their identifiers behind the scenes.
body: Home Assistant’s automation editor lets people choose which trigger an action depends on directly from the “Triggered by” condition. It shows the triggers themselves and creates an identifier when needed, removing the preliminary job of inventing names and matching them by hand.

Existing explicit identifiers remain supported in YAML. Automations that share one identifier across several triggers receive an optional repair: after confirmation, each trigger gets a distinct identifier and the condition keeps matching the same set of events. Templates that use the identifier directly can still need manual adjustment.

Jan-Philipp Benecke implements the approach shaped by Niels, with design work from Marcin Bauer and approval recorded by Franck Nijhof. The interface puts the previously approved roadmap plan into practice.
articles.continuity: The September 9 edition covered the approved plan; this work supplies the trigger-selection interface.

articles.title: Home Assistant restores network settings from encrypted backups
articles.dek: Saved storage connections recover after a restore had silently skipped them.
body: A Home Assistant backup could report a successful restore while silently leaving out its network storage connections and Docker registry settings. Supervisor corrects the way it reads those settings from an encrypted backup, recovering information that was present but never applied.

The failure affects encrypted backups containing Supervisor settings since Supervisor 2026.03.3. Stefan Agner says the saved settings remain intact and can be recovered by restoring again with the correction. His companion Core fix also encrypts or decrypts those settings when preparing a download or moving a backup between locations with different encryption choices.

Encrypt and decrypt supervisor.tar in backup rewrites

articles.title: Home Assistant shows which Hue scene a room is using
articles.dek: A room or zone gains one selector for regular and smart scenes, with the active choice kept in view.
body: Philips Hue households gain a way to see and change the scene active in each room or zone from Home Assistant. A new selector lists the group’s regular scenes and scheduled smart scenes together and follows the scene currently in use.

When a smart scene and the regular scene it is running are both active, the selector shows the smart scene. The feature supports Hue v2 bridges; capturing a scene for later restoration remains separate follow-up work.
Steven makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the feature.

articles.title: Music Assistant closes a route around local-file permissions
articles.dek: Its built-in source accepts remote links, leaving server files behind the administrator-controlled filesystem source.
body: Music Assistant closes a route that could read music or image files anywhere its server process could reach. The built-in source previously accepted a local file path where it expected a track, radio stream or image link, bypassing the administrator-only setup for local music folders.
Marcel van der Veldt restricts that source to remote URLs. Local files remain available through a filesystem music source set up and shared by an administrator.

articles.title: ESPHome keeps muted speakers quiet when the volume changes
articles.dek: Zero volume stays silent, while smoother software volume changes remove audible clicks.
body: ESPHome speakers keep their mute setting when someone adjusts the volume. Setting the level to zero stays silent, including on setups with a configured minimum volume or a separate audio converter. One failure could bring sound back when someone pressed volume-down again after reaching zero, while the player still reported that it was muted.

Software-controlled speakers also fade between volume levels, removing clicks when volume or mute changes. A full mute takes about a tenth of a second. Automations need to account for the separation: setting volume to zero no longer reports mute or fires mute and unmute triggers. A speaker connected to an audio converter should control its mute setting itself.
Kevin Ahrendt contributes the coordinated changes alongside Carrie Watts and rexmoriarty, who each make their first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Music Assistant finds the replacement after a Plex music upgrade
articles.dek: Library synchronization removes dead links that could keep upgraded albums from playing.
body: Replacing music files with better copies in Plex could leave Music Assistant trying to play the deleted originals. Library synchronization removes those stale links when the source reports its current collection, so a metadata match no longer leaves a dead copy competing with its replacement.

RyanAtTanagra found 600 of 2,324 album links pointing to deleted items after upgrading a Plex library to FLAC. The cleanup follows the library-sync deletion setting, waits for a complete synchronization and preserves items the source says it skipped. Streaming-service catalogs and Music Assistant’s direct local-files source are outside this cleanup.
This is RyanAtTanagra’s first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by Marcel van der Veldt.

articles.title: Assist recognizes natural apostrophes in Italian and French
articles.dek: Its language matcher accepts joined articles and stops stray transcript punctuation blocking commands.
body: The language matcher behind Assist recognizes Italian and French phrases whose articles join the next word with an apostrophe. Natural wording such as the Italian “nell’ingresso” could fail unless an unnatural space followed the apostrophe, even though the language rules already allowed the normal spelling.

Martino Dell’Ambrogio corrects the word boundary in Hassil, covering straight and curly apostrophes in his first contribution to the library. Michael Hansen also makes it ignore stray dashes and ellipses at word boundaries, including a trailing dash that Soniox sometimes adds to a transcript. Hyphens inside words and minus signs before negative numbers keep their meaning.

articles.title: De Dietrich boiler readings join Home Assistant locally
articles.dek: The new integration starts with read-only Diematic sensors through a serial-to-network gateway.
body: De Dietrich Diematic heating systems gain a Home Assistant integration for reading their measurements locally. The read-only integration connects through an RS485-to-network gateway; it does not yet provide heating controls.

Daan Vervacke tested an iSystem installation reporting the D4 type. The supporting library also knows Diematic 3 and Diematic 4 layouts, but those still require testing on real equipment. Vervacke makes his first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the integration.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s live Energy view includes water-only homes
articles.dek: Live water or gas monitoring no longer needs an electricity power sensor to open the Now tab.
body: A household monitoring live water or gas flow can use Home Assistant’s Energy “Now” view without also adding an electricity power sensor. The dashboard had hidden the tab from those setups even though the view already knew how to show their readings.
Petar Petrov makes the tab follow the live measurements available. A flow-rate sensor is still required; the change does not create a live measurement from a consumption total.

pullRequests.title: Show Energy Now view for water and gas flow without power sensors

articles.title: Home Assistant stops a pending Supervisor update holding up the rest
articles.dek: Discovering a new Supervisor version starts its automatic update instead of waiting for the daily check.
body: Opening Home Assistant Settings could discover a Supervisor update and then block Home Assistant, operating-system and app updates until the next daily task installed it. Supervisor starts its automatic update whenever its version information refreshes while the system is running, closing that waiting period.

Paulus Schoutsen also makes a manual update request share an automatic update already in progress, avoiding a competing-job error. A backup restore that needs a newer Supervisor distinguishes an update under way from one that cannot start automatically.

pullRequests.title: Start the Supervisor auto update on every version reload

roadmapUpdates.title: Forecast plans look beyond the spot price
roadmapUpdates.summary: Home Assistant is shaping sensor forecasts. Markus Tuominen says he wants later template-based forecasts to include electricity margins and transfer tariffs; the initial proposal remains limited to one forecast per sensor, with uncertainty displays left for later.
